gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-marche: Noto Sans Marchen stands tall and open, its small letters almost capital-sized. Almendra Display handles the ornate, literary flourish up top, while the sans-serif body does the quiet, clear work of being read.
gen-eater-gf-prompt: Menacing and jagged, Eater spaces its letters wide and keeps its thin strokes close to its stems in weight. Prompt stays approachable.
gen-flavors-gf-pt-sans-caption: Whimsical and loud, Flavors towers with a stubby, marker-traced x-height, while PT Sans Caption keeps its bowls unclosed and inviting. Big gestures meet easy lowercase.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-puritan: Expressive curves in Autour One run without any tapering where strokes meet or end, giving it a blunt, confident roundness. And Puritan, a plain sans, keeps its forms open to the side, so a long passage would feel easygoing.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-questrial: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, and that is where it commands attention best. But Questrial, a plain sans, does its best work in the tall band of lowercase with short stalks above.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, futuristic and round-pen smooth. Noto Sans Tagalog then fills the line with a dominant middle zone, so a long passage would read generously open.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-medefa: Noto Sans Medefaidrin reads crisp, its lowercase rising high with no ink pooling where curves turn in. And Almendra Display brings ornate, literary letters on top, so give the sans a modest size and let the heading stay lofty.
gen-eater-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada, a plain sans, reads steadily, with tall, full c, s and z and a clear opening at every curve. Give it a moderate size, since Eater already supplies the menace.
gen-flavors-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big fills its line with a tall x-height and terminals that finish well clear of the stem, tracing a monoline skeleton. Flavors earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-gabarito-archivo: Distinctive and expressive, Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Archivo, the sans-serif partner, does its best work with a commanding x-height and curves that open outward.
